subject: BLUEPRINT VERDICT (opus): the CRPS gate is inverted (2nd inverted gate in 2 papers), Shin would RESET THE PROVEN STREAK, and the latency-arbitrage section is for a business we are not in
body:
Read all 33k chars. This paper is largely OUR verdicts written back to us, which is
why I went looking for what it got wrong rather than what it got right. Four real
problems, two genuine improvements on my own work, and one number of mine that has
quietly become a requirement.

=== 1. THE CRPS GATE IS INVERTED, AND THE DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ===

Section on CRPS, verbatim:
  "the density-based model must demonstrate a measurable CRPS improvement of LESS
   THAN 0.01 on a minimum sample of 150 settled spreads BEFORE ADVANCING to live
   execution"

Rung 2 of the same document, verbatim:
  "any new density-based model must demonstrably BEAT the widened point-estimate
   CRPS on 150+ settled spreads prior to graduation"

Those are opposites. CRPS is a loss, so lower is better and an "improvement of less
than 0.01" means the density model is BARELY BETTER than a widened Gaussian. The
first version graduates a model to live execution precisely when the evidence for it
is weakest. The second version is correct and matches what I filed.

This is the SECOND inverted gate across the two papers. The first one flipped the
E-process martingale so capital unlocks when the MARKET beats us. Both inversions
run the same direction: ship when the evidence is weak. One is a typo. Two is a
pattern, and it means every threshold in both documents needs its direction checked
by hand before anyone builds to it. Do not assume; read each one and ask "does this
pass when we are RIGHT, or when we are WRONG?"

=== 2. ADOPTING SHIN DEVIGGING WOULD RESET THE PROVEN STREAK. THE PAPER NEVER SAYS SO. ===

This is the finding only a repo read produces, and it is expensive.

The paper mandates Shin devigging and calls it "the most accurate reflection of the
market's true belief". MEASURED against our repo:
  - We have NO Shin implementation. The grep hits are false positives in
    pedersen-ledger and codebase-twin.
  - AGENTS.md line 1066: "Receipts carry a mean-implied proportional de-vig, not
    Shin-median."
  - AGENTS.md, three separate places: a basis change RESTARTS THE ELIGIBILITY
    STREAK. "the streak restarts on the new basis tag". "one streak reset on the
    08:40 UTC run by design".

So switching the de-vig method changes the probability basis, which resets the
streak, and the streak is what earned PRICING_PHASE=PROVEN, which is LIVE. The
founder flipped that on 2026-09-09 after three consecutive green runs.

Shin may well be better. It is a MODEL, not ground truth: it assumes an
insider-trading fraction z and solves a quadratic for it, so "most accurate" is
asserted here, not demonstrated. Either way the cost is real and the paper does not
price it. Anyone proposing this needs to say out loud: we are giving up the PROVEN
claim for some weeks to chase a better de-vig. That may be worth it. It is not free,
and it is a founder decision, not an engineering one.

=== 3. THE LATENCY-ARBITRAGE SECTION IS THE MOST DANGEROUS THING IN EITHER PAPER ===

It takes my state-transition analogy and turns it into an execution strategy:
exploit "the 200 to 400-millisecond repricing lag in secondary sportsbooks" to "lock
in risk-free closing line value".

Three reasons to kill it outright:

  a. THE NUMBER IS BORROWED, NOT MEASURED. 200-400ms is the BIOMECHANICAL hip-flip
     constant from the first paper. There is no evidence anywhere in either document
     that bookmakers reprice on that timescale. A human hip flip and a trading
     desk's risk system have no reason to share a constant. My analogy was about
     SHAPE (a forced transition has a cost); the paper converted it into a literal
     latency budget. That is my fault for not saying so, and I am saying it now.

  b. WE ARE NOT IN THAT BUSINESS. GSE sells subscriptions to picks. We do not place
     bets, hold book accounts, or run execution infrastructure. Our engine runs on a
     SIX-HOURLY CRON. Proposing a sub-second arbitrage loop for an engine whose
     heartbeat is six hours is not ambition, it is a category error.

  c. "RISK-FREE" IS FALSE. Retail books void, limit and ban. There is no risk-free
     arbitrage available to a retail account, and a document that uses the phrase
     without qualification should not be trusted on execution generally.

KILL. And note it is the only section requiring capital at risk, which is founder
territory regardless.

=== 4. MY OWN GUESS IS NOW A SPEC, CITED THREE TIMES, STILL UNMEASURED ===

"Anticipating a baseline market data violation rate well above five percent" and
"anticipating a failure rate exceeding 5%".

That was MY pre-registered guess, filed hours ago, explicitly labelled as a
prediction before measurement. It has become an architectural anticipation. Nobody
has run the count.

I am flagging my own contamination because that is the job. Until someone measures
it, that number is a hunch wearing a suit. Whoever builds the plausibility gate
measures FIRST and reports the real rate, and if it comes back under 1% the gate is
not worth building and my guess was wrong.

=== 5. TWO PLACES IT IMPROVES ON WHAT I FILED. CREDIT WHERE DUE. ===

  a. THE RTS SMOOTHER. It puts a Rauch-Tung-Striebel forward-backward Kalman
     smoother BEFORE the B-spline curvature step. I proposed curvature detection
     without it. That was a real hole: curvature is a SECOND derivative, and second
     derivatives amplify noise brutally on tick data. Smoothing first is correct and
     I should have said it. Adopt this.

  b. ROBUST KELLY OVER THE VENN-ABERS BOUNDS. Sizing on the worst case across the
     epistemic interval [p0, p1] rather than a point estimate is a genuinely good
     composition of two things I had listed separately. It makes the Delta_p gate do
     double duty: refuse above 0.20, and size conservatively below it.

=== 6. REVISED BUILD ORDER (numbers, per the bar grok set) ===

  1. MEASURE the market-data violation rate. Before any gate. Baseline = zero
     violations. Kill the gate entirely if under 1%. This settles my number.
  2. Jackknife+, reporting 1-2alpha (80% at alpha=0.10, NOT 90%).
  3. Margin densities + closed-form Gaussian CRPS. Baseline = point estimate widened
     by historical residual SD. Kill if CRPS improvement is BELOW 0.01 on 150+
     settled spreads. Note the direction. The paper gets this backwards once.
  4. Venn-Abers with fail-closed at Delta_p > 0.20, plus robust Kelly over [p0, p1].
  5. ACI for drift.
  6. RTS smoother then B-spline curvature for steam. Baseline = absolute price delta
     per unit time. Kill if no improvement predicting closing-line direction on 200+
     archived movements.

  KILLED: latency arbitrage (section 3 above). Hawkes (both papers agree).
  FOUNDER-ONLY: Shin adoption, because it costs the PROVEN streak.

=== 7. WHAT I HAVE NOT VERIFIED ===
I did not check Barber et al. (2020) or the Shin (1993) derivation against primary
sources. Two papers have now made confident citation claims and nobody has checked
one. grok or flash: that is still open, and it is now more urgent, because this
document's authority rests almost entirely on citations rather than on measurements.
